newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Rafsanjani sees no thaw in ties with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Iran's Rafsanjani sees no thaw in ties with U.S..

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, approaching the end of his tenure, said on Wednesday he could not foresee any easing in strained relations with the United States.

"I do not predict any development (in the relations). The situation between us and America has not changed in several years and I do not see any other prospects in the future," Rafsanjani told a news conference in Tehran.

Iran has rejected Western media reports linking it to the bombing of a U.S. military complex in Saudi Arabia in June that killed 19 American airmen. Some Tehran officials have said the reports indicated that Washington was preparing to attack Iran.

"I do not think it is probable that the (U.S.) threats will become reality. The Americans know Iran and we have shown Iran's power, defence capabilities and morale in the past. We are not afraid. Whoever commits aggression will be the loser," he said.

"There have been no official messages sent by America to threaten us. It does not address us like that. It sends verbal messages through the Swiss embassy when it feels threatened over its interests in northern Iraq or in Lebanon," Rafsanjani said.
Iran has repeatedly asked the United States to release its frozen assets in U.S. banks which it puts at about $12 billion.
Washington froze the sums after the 1979 Islamic revolution when militants seized the U.S. embassy in Tehran and took its staff hostage. It says the amount is in the hundred of millions of dollars.

"America lacks goodwill. If it proves it has goodwill, they will see a different face of Iran. If they return the money they owe us from before the revolution, our monies which have been blocked, I would see that as a proof of goodwill," Rafsanjani said.
Washington has launched an economic and political campaign to isolate Tehran, accusing it of supporting terrorism and seeking to obtain nuclear weapons.
Iran denies the charges and accuses the United States of being bent on destroying its Islamic government.
Rafsanjani's tenure as president ends in August. He is barred by the constitution from seeking a third consecutive four-year term.
